content:
cami: Heads-up — we want to migrate staging KeyVaults from access policies -> RBAC next week. Main concerns: envelope (DEK) rotation behavior, audit visibility for wrap/unwrap, and the cross-tenant managed identity used by Dedicated. Anyone hit surprises during a cutover?

thomas: +1 this. biggest gotcha we hit before was role granularity: you need crypto-specific permissions (wrap/unwrap/sign) explicitly. also watch user-assigned vs system-assigned MI semantics.

maria: For migration order, don't delete access policies before RBAC is fully in place. If an app still references an SP or managed identity that lost access you get silent unwrap failures. We did a staged approach: create RBAC role assignment for the MI, test, then remove access policy.

leo: Audit question — are we confident the vault diagnostics give enough context to correlate wrapKey calls back to requests? In our on-prem private deployment we saw wrap/unwrap events but no caller IP and the app-level request id wasn't included by default.

sre-bot: deploy-log: staging/kv-migration started by @cami at 2025-09-14T15:02:00Z.

thomas: For audit: enable diagnostic settings to send to Log Analytics and to a Storage account (archival). Event schema includes authorization.action (e.g., Microsoft.KeyVault/keys/wrap/action) and caller in claims. Make sure to set "Include request body" in any custom ingestion if you need correlation ids.

maria: Example CLI for role assignment we used:
```
az role assignment create \\n  --assignee <MI_PRINCIPAL_ID> \\n  --role "Azure Key Vault Crypto Service Encryption User" \\n  --scope /subscriptions/<sub>/resourceGroups/<rg>/providers/Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/my-kv/keys/my-key
```
Note: that role scope can be the specific key resource which avoids wide permissions.

leo: Regarding envelope rotation: app flow is DEK (data key) stored in our app DB encrypted with AKV key (KEK). On rotation we create new key version, re-wrap DEK with new key, update DB, then invalidate local caches. Important: keep previous key versions available for a window and enable soft-delete + purge protection so rollback works.

cami: What about Dedicated's cross-tenant MI? we use guest principals across customer tenant boundaries, sometimes the MI mapping fails after conversion to RBAC. Do we need SP fallback?

thomas: Guest MI is flaky across tenant boundaries. Pattern that worked for us: 1) provision a user-assigned MI in the vault tenant and grant it RBAC on the key, 2) in the consuming tenant use a service principal that you mint via our onboarding automation and federate it to the consuming app's identity. Avoid relying on system-assigned MIs when crossing tenants.

maria: If you must use an SP fallback, ensure its certificate/secret rotation is automated and immediately test unwrap. Also add an AAD conditional MFA/exp policy so stale secrets can't be used.

leo: Ops checklist we followed for dry-run:
- enable diagnostics to both LA and storage
- create RBAC assignments scoped to keys
- run a small batch rotation in staging: create new key version -> rewrap 5 DEKs -> update apps -> confirm unwraps for all
- verify metrics and count of Microsoft.KeyVault/keys/wrap/action in LA
- test rollback by re-establishing previous key version and unwrapping sample DEKs

engsec-bot: reminder: KV soft delete and purge protection must be on for rotation window per security policy.

cami: Quick note on multi-cloud envelope flows — some customers use AKV to wrap DEKs but store ciphertext in AWS S3. If we migrate RBAC, make sure the cross-cloud service principal used for tooling still has unwrap rights. We saw ops tooling break because the CI runner used an SP that was only in access policies.

thomas: Good call — we should enumerate any automation/CI consumers that use access policies and update them before cutover. Also add a feature flag in apps to retry unwrap with previous key version for N minutes.

maria: Logging tip: query Log Analytics with something like:
```
AzureDiagnostics 
| where OperationName contains "wrap" or OperationName contains "unwrap" 
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, Identity, CorrelationId, ResultDescription
| sort by TimeGenerated desc
```
This helped us find the CI runner misconfig.

cami: Action items: thomas to create runbook + CLI snippets for scoped role assignment; leo to run a staged rotation in staging and report unwrap success rates; maria to inventory automation consumers using access policies. I'll coordinate scheduling. Who can run the dry-run Thurs?

thomas: I can run the runbook Thurs morning.

leo: I'll start the staged rotation after AM smoke tests.

maria: I'll produce the consumer list by EOD Wed.

cami: Thanks all — I'll update the migration PR with the runbook link and add diagnostic queries. :thumbsup:
